PIT fundamentals, macro, exchange APIs, on-chain data and archives, each with authority tier and fre

# quantitativeTrading-source-reliable
English · 简体中文
Source reliability for quantitative finance and crypto trading in DeepSeek Harness: a bundled regist
ry of **119 curated, agent-collectable sources** with authority tiers, verification states, five-sta
te point-in-time flags, revision-risk and per-source dataset tags, plus two model-facing tools to fi
nd sources and audit citations with match confidence and credential redaction.
A plugin for DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`). The registry ships as data; both tools are local lookups (no
network calls), so they are fast and have no side effects. It is independent from `cs-source-reliabl
e` and can be installed on its own.
## What it ships
- **119 sources** — 73 `quant` (filings, macro, fundamentals, China A-share/HK, execution, global of
ficial statistics) and 46 `crypto` (exchanges, derivatives, on-chain, archives, SDKs, news, ETF flow

s).
- Per source: domain, category, authority tier (`A` regulator/exchange/official docs, `B` instit
utional vendor/peer-reviewed, `C` curated secondary, `D` lead only), evidence type, `content_access`
, `verification` (`discovered` / `reachable` / `schema_verified` / `semantic_verified` / `production
_approved`), `license_class`, `cache_policy`, `attribution`, `refresh_days`, `last_checked`, `pit` (
`yes` / `partial` / `no` / `not_applicable` / `unverified`), `revision_risk` (`none` / `rare` / `pos
sible` / `routine` / `unknown`), `data_types` (dataset tags), `redistribution` (`allowed` / `restric
ted` / `prohibited` / `unknown`), and where verified `rate_limit`, `license_url`, `freshness_sla`, `

fallback_id`, plus `free_tier`, `auth`, `iface`, `history_start`.
- `data_types` is a controlled voc
abulary (`data/datasets.yaml`, 87 tags); `tools/build-data.cjs` rejects unknown tags, bad ids, bad e

nums and dangling `fallback_id`.
- `api_hosts` maps real API endpoint hosts to the source that docum
ents them (22 sources, e.g. `fapi.binance.com` → `binance-futures-api`), so a genuine API URL is att

ributed even when the docs live on another host.
- A curation layer (`data/enrichment.yaml`, version
2) records what was verified after the probe — PIT corrections, verification states, revision-risk

overrides, optional attributes and per-source dataset tags.
- `sources.json` carries `meta.data_vers

ion: 2` and `meta.build` (built_at, source_count, matrix/enrichment/dataset versions).
- **Two tools

**: `qt_source_find` and `qt_source_audit`.
- A short system-prompt section (order 241) that tells t
he model when to use them and how to cite.
## It exists because the common advice is subtly wrong
Everything below was checked against the official page or API on **2026-11-06**; the probe snapshot
is stored per source in the YAML matrices.
| Common claim | What the registry records instead |
| "Massive (formerly Polygon.io)" | True — `polygon.io` redirects to `massive.com`; personal pricing

showed `$199/mo`. |
| "Alpha Vantage free tier is fine for a prototype" | Free tier is **25 request

s/day**; premium starts at **$49.99/mo**. Useless for an agent loop. |
| "Alpaca data is free to sta
rt" | Free tier API data is **15-minute delayed**; real-time SIP requires **Algo Trader Plus $99/mo*

*. |
| "Twelve Data free tier" | **8 credits/min, 800/day**; Grow is **$79/mo**. |
[该节后续省略]
### What the flags mean
- `pit` describes whether PIT is the right control: `not_applicable` means PIT does not fit this sou
rce (raw ticks/snapshots, tooling, sandbox) — it does **not** mean history never changes; `unverifie

d` means nobody checked.
- `revision_risk` is the second dimension: `none` (official raw archives ob
served without rebuild), `rare` (on-chain reorgs/backfills), `possible` (aggregators, vendor rebuild
s, news corrections), `routine` (macro/fundamentals revised often), `unknown`. Build derives a categ

ory default; `data/enrichment.yaml` records verified exceptions.
- `verification` is separate from `
authority`: `reachable` only means HTTP 200 from the probe network; `schema_verified` means a payloa
d shape was seen; `semantic_verified` means a specific fee/limit/endpoint/PIT claim was checked; `pr
oduction_approved` means it was used end-to-end; `discovered` means the page was unreachable at prob

e time and is a citation lead only.
- `data_types` names the datasets a source actually covers, so a
citation can be matched to the dataset it claims (depth, aggTrades, funding, OI, XBRL, vintages, …)

.
- `redistribution` is a policy bucket derived from `license_class` (public-domain/open-source → al

lowed, site terms → restricted, unknown otherwise); it is not legal advice.
- For news and event-dri
ven facts cite the first publication time; a page update time is not evidence.
## Limitations
- The tools **look up a curated registry**; they do not fetch pages, call APIs, or verify claims on

their own.
- `qt_source_audit` is a mechanical check (URL extraction, match confidence, tier mapping

, uncited-paragraph count). It does not judge whether a cited source actually supports a sentence.
-
Redaction covers common credential parameter names and userinfo; a nonstandard parameter name may p

ass through. The raw URL is used for matching and is not logged by the plugin.
- `same_host_ambiguou
s` matches are reported as not known; a legitimate deep link that is not registered will stay ambigu

ous until the registry records it.
- `api_host` attribution maps the host only; it does not prove th

at the cited endpoint path or parameters are the documented ones.
- A/B tiers reduce risk; they do n
ot guarantee correctness. `verification` records what was checked and when — `reachable` is not a da

ta-quality score. Fees, limits and endpoints change — re-probe before relying on a number.
- Non-reg

istry URLs are flagged as unknown even when legitimate.
- The plugin does not execute trades, store
API keys, or give legal/compliance advice. Trading requires a deterministic risk layer between the m
odel and the exchange.
